# Analyze yellowtail catch patterns by season and DOY
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

trips = tables['trips']

# Focus on multi-day classes (day_1_5, overnight) that show strong October yields
multi_day = trips[trips['cls'].isin(['day_1_5', 'overnight', 'full_day'])].copy()

# Calculate share by season and fishing doy for yellowtail
multi_day['share'] = multi_day['yt'] / (multi_day['anglers'] + 1)

# Group by season, doy, and class
seasonal_doy = multi_day.groupby(['fish_date_season', 'fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'share': ['sum', 'mean', 'count'],
    'anglers': 'sum'
}).reset_index()

seasonal_doy.columns = ['season', 'doy', 'cls', 'yt_total', 'share_total', 'share_mean', 'trip_count', 'anglers_total']

# Focus on Oct window (doy ~280-310)
oct_window = seasonal_doy[(seasonal_doy['doy'] >= 280) & (seasonal_doy['doy'] <= 310)].copy()
oct_window = oct_window.sort_values(['doy', 'cls'])

print("October peak window (doy 280-310) by class:")
print("\nDay_1_5 trips:")
print(oct_window[oct_window['cls'] == 'day_1_5'][['season', 'doy', 'trip_count', 'yt_total', 'share_mean']].to_string())
print("\nOvernight trips:")
print(oct_window[oct_window['cls'] == 'overnight'][['season', 'doy', 'trip_count', 'yt_total', 'share_mean']].to_string())

# Summary statistics by class across all October windows
print("\n\nSummary: Average share by class across Oct windows (all seasons):")
for cls in ['day_1_5', 'overnight']:
    subset = multi_day[(multi_day['fish_date_doy'] >= 280) & (multi_day['fish_date_doy'] <= 310) & (multi_day['cls'] == cls)]
    avg_share = subset['share'].mean()
    trip_count = len(subset)
    print(f"{cls}: {avg_share:.3f} yt/angler avg ({trip_count} trips)")
